P = h/λ

K = P²/(2m) = hν − φ

where P is momentum, K is kinetic energy, h is Planck's constant, m is mass of electron, ν is frequency, and φ is work function.

From K = P²/(2m) = hν − φ:

P²/(2m) = hν − φ

P = h/λ, so:

h²/(λ²·2m) = hν − φ

hν = φ + h²/(2mλ²)

ν = φ/h + h/(2mλ²)

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Consider the reactions
A.sol_text:
Answer: (3) Functional isomers

Solution:

Starting material: Phenyl-CH₂-Br (benzyl bromide)

Path 1 (via AgCN):
Phenyl-CH₂-Br + AgCN → Phenyl-CH₂-NC (isocyanide)
Phenyl-CH₂-NC + LiAlH₄ → (A) Phenyl-CH₂-NH-CH₃ (N-methylbenzylamine)

Path 2 (via KCN):
Phenyl-CH₂-Br + KCN → Phenyl-CH₂-CN (nitrile)
Phenyl-CH₂-CN + LiAlH₄ → (B) Phenyl-CH₂-CH₂-NH₂ (2-phenylethylamine)

Product A: C₆H₅-CH₂-NH-CH₃ (secondary amine with molecular formula C₈H₁₁N)
Product B: C₆H₅-CH₂-CH₂-NH₂ (primary amine with molecular formula C₈H₁₁N)

A and B have the same molecular formula (C₈H₁₁N) but different functional groups:
- A contains a secondary amine (R₂NH)
- B contains a primary amine (RCH₂NH₂)

Since they have the same molecular formula but different functional groups, A and B are functional isomers.

A.text:
Match the reactions in Column-I with appropriate options in Column-II.

(A) CH₃ — C — H with H above C and O double bonded below C, treated with (i) LiAlH₄/ether (ii) H₃O⁺ → (P) CH₃ — CH₂ — CH₃

(B) CH₃ — C — H with O double bonded below C, treated with Zn — Hg / HCl → (Q) CH₃ — CH₂ — OH

(C) CH₃ — C — C — CH₃ with C₂H₅ above the first C, H below the first C, and O double bonded below the second C, treated with NaBH₄ → (R) CH₃ — CH₃

(D) CH₃ — C — CH₃ with O double bonded below C, treated with HI / Red P / Δ → (S) CH₃ — CH — C — CH₃ with C₂H₅ and H above/below the middle C and OH below the last C

(1) (A) → R, (B) → Q, (C) → S, (D) → P
(2) (A) → Q, (B) → R, (C) → P, (D) → S
(3) (A) → Q, (B) → R, (C) → S, (D) → P
(4) (A) → R, (B) → Q, (C) → P, (D) → S
A.sol_text:
(A) CH₃ — C — H with H above C and O double bonded below, treated with (i) LiAlH₄ (ii) H₃O⁺ → CH₃ — CH — H with OH below
This is reduction of an aldehyde to a primary alcohol using LiAlH₄, giving CH₃ — CH₂ — OH, which is (Q)

(B) CH₃ — C — H with O double bonded below, treated with Zn — Hg / HCl → CH₃ — CH₃ (Clemmensen reduction)
This is Clemmensen reduction of an aldehyde to an alkane, giving CH₃ — CH₃, which is (R)

(C) CH₃ — C — C — CH₃ with C₂H₅ above first C, H below first C, and O double bonded below second C, treated with NaBH₄ → CH₃ — C — C — CH₃ with C₂H₅ and H above/below middle C and OH below
NaBH₄ reduces the carbonyl group to an alcohol, giving a secondary alcohol, which is (S)

(D) CH₃ — C — CH₃ with O double bonded below, treated with HI / Red P / Δ → CH₃ — CH₂ — CH₃
This is Clemmensen reduction (HI/Red P is equivalent) of a ketone to an alkane, giving propane, which is (P)

Therefore: (A) → Q, (B) → R, (C) → S, (D) → P

B.text: Resistance of 0.2 M solution of an electrolyte is 50 Ω. The specific conductance of the solution is 1.3 S m⁻¹. If resistance of the 0.4 M solution of the same electrolyte is 260 Ω and its molar conductivity is a × 10⁻⁶ Sm² mol⁻¹, the value of a/25 is-

= (1/260) × (S × 65 m⁻¹)/(0.4 mol litre⁻¹)

= 6.25 × 10⁻⁴ S m² mol⁻¹

Let f: (-π/2, π/2) → ℝ be a differentiable function such that
lim(t→x) [f(x)tan t - f(t)tan x]/(t - x) = -e^(-x)tan^2 x for all x ∈ (-π/2, π/2). If f(π/4) = e^(-π/4), then which one of the following is true?
options: f(x) has a local maxima at x = 0
f(x) has exactly one extremum point in (-π/2, π/2)
A.sol_text:
lim(t→x) [f(x)sec t - f(t)tan x]/1 = -x tan^2 x
⇒ f(x)sec^2 x - f'(x)tan x = e^(-x)tan^2 x
⇒ [-f(x)sec^2 x + f'(x)tan x]/(tan^2 x) = -e^(-x)
⇒ d/dx[f(x)/tan x] = -e^(-x)
⇒ f(x)/tan x = e^(-x) + C
⇒ f(π/4) = e^(-π/4) + C
⇒ e^(-π/4) = e^(-π/4) + 6
⇒ C = 0
⇒ f(x) = (tan x)e^(-x)
= e^(-x)(tan^2 x - tan x + 1)
⇒ f'(x) > 0 ∀x ∈ ℝ
⇒ f(x) is increasing in (-π/2, π/2)

A.text: The function f(x) = [x] + √{x}; where [x] and {x} are integral and fractional part of x, then
options: f(x) is non-differentiable at all integers
f(x) is discontinuous at all integers
f(x) is discontinuous at x = 0 only
A.sol_text:
Answer : (2)
Solution:

y = [x]
[Graph showing step function with open circles at integer values and closed circles just before each integer]

y = √{x}
[Graph showing repeating curve segments starting at each integer, forming a sawtooth-like pattern]

y = [x] + √{x}
[Graph showing combined function with jumps at integers and smooth curves between them]

The function f(x) = [x] + √{x} consists of:
- [x]: the greatest integer function, which is discontinuous at all integers
- √{x}: the square root of the fractional part, which is continuous

At integer values of x, [x] has jump discontinuities. The fractional part {x} equals 0 at integers, making √{x} = 0 at these points.

At each integer n:
- The left limit involves the previous integer's fractional part approaching 1
- The right limit has the fractional part starting from 0
- This creates a jump discontinuity at each integer

Therefore, f(x) is non-differentiable at all integers because the function is discontinuous at these points.

x(c/t - ct³ + t²x) = -c²

A.text: If z₁, z₂ are complex numbers such that Re(z₁) = |z₁-1|, Re(z₂) = |z₂-1|, and arg(z₁-z₂) = π/6, then Im(z₁ + z₂) is equal to-
A.sol_text:
Let z₁ = x₁ + iy₁, z₂ = x₂ + iy₂
⇒ x₁ = √((x₁-1)² + y₁²)
⇒ x₁² = x₁² + 1 - 2x₁ + y₁²
⇒ y₁² - 2x₁ + 1 = 0
...(i)
Similarly
y₂² - 2x₂ + 1 = 0
...(ii)
Now
(i) - (ii), (y₁ - y₂)(y₁ + y₂) = 2(x₁ - x₂)
⇒ y₁ - y₂ = 2(x₁ - x₂)/(y₁ + y₂) ⇒ (y₁ - y₂)/(x₁ - x₂) = 2/(y₁ + y₂)
Now
arg(z₁ - z₂) = π/6
tan⁻¹((y₁ - y₂)/(x₁ - x₂)) = π/6
(y₁ - y₂)/(x₁ - x₂) = 1/√3
⇒ 2/(y₁ + y₂) = 1/√3
⇒ y₁ + y₂ = 2√3
So I_M = (z₁ + z₂) = y₁ + y₂ = 2√3

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: A fair die is rolled four times. The probability that each of the final three rolls is at least as large as the roll preceding it expressed in the form m/n, where gcd(m, n) = 1. Then, the value of m + n is
B.sol_text:
If we take any combinations of four numbers, there is only one way to order them in a non-descending order. The dice rolls can be in the form:

ABCD
AABC
AABB
AAAB
AAAA

(i) For first case, there are ⁶C₄ = 15 ways.

(ii) For second case, ⁶C₃ = 20 ways to pick 3 numbers, ³C₁ ways to pick 1 to duplicate
= ⁶C₃ · ³C₁
= 60 ways

(iii) For third case, ⁶C₂ ways to pick 2 numbers. We will duplicate both.

(iv) For fourth case, ⁶C₂ ways to pick 2 numbers, ²C₁ ways to pick 1 to duplicate
= 15 · 2
= 30 ways

(v) For fifth case, ⁶C₁ = 6 ways

∴ m/n = (15 + 60 + 15 + 30 + 6)/(6⁴)
= 126/(6⁴)
= 7/72

∴ m + n = 79
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.text: For a data of n observations x₁, x₂, …, xₙ, if Σᵢ₌₁ⁿ(2xᵢ+1)² = 29n and Σᵢ₌₁ⁿ(3xᵢ-1)² = 34n, then the variance of this data is-
B.sol_text:
Hint:
σ² = (Σx²ᵢ)/N - (Σxᵢ/N)²

Solution:
Σ(2xᵢ+1)² = 29n
⇒ 4A + n + 4B = 29n
⇒ A + B = 7n
Where A = Σⁿᵢ₌₁ x²ᵢ, B = Σⁿᵢ₌₁ xᵢ

Σ(3xᵢ-1)² = 34n
⇒ 9A + n - 6B = 34n
⇒ 3A - 2B = 11n
∴ A = 5n, B = 2n

σ² = (1/n)Σx²ᵢ - (1/n Σxᵢ)²
= A/n - B²/n²
= 5n/n - (2n)²/n²
= 5 - 4 = 1
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.text: Let P, Q be points on the ellipse 16x² + 25y² = 400 so that PQ = 96/25 and P, Q lie above major axis. The circle drawn with PQ as diameter touches major axis at focus with positive abscissa. If m is slope of PQ, then the value of 17m² is equal to
B.sol_text:
Eccentricity of given ellipse = 3/5
∴ Focus of ellipse = (3, 0)

Equation of required circle is x² + y² - 6x + λy + 9 = 0
Where λ is an arbitrary constant

∴ r = √(9 + λ²/4 - 9) = 48/25

⇒ λ = ±96/25, (λ = 96/25 is rejected)

∴ Centre of circle = (3, 48/25)

∴ Equation of chord with given mid point is x + y = 123/25

∴ Slope of PQ = -1

∴ 17m² = 17.
